title: Trigonometric Equations and General Values
notes: ### 1. Why the solution is a family
Sine, cosine, and tangent repeat, so a trigonometric equation has infinitely many solutions. The general solution lists all of them with an integer n.
If sin θ = sin α, then θ = nπ + (−1)^n α. The factor (−1)^n switches between the two solutions in each period of 2π.
If cos θ = cos α, then θ = 2nπ ± α. Cosine is even about zero, so both +α and −α appear in every full turn.
If tan θ = tan α, then θ = nπ + α. Tangent has period π, so adding nπ gives every solution, and there is no extra ±.

Rewrite the equation as sin θ = sin α, cos θ = cos α, or tan θ = tan α before using a general solution. Discard any value that lies outside the asked interval, and test any root that was introduced by squaring.
keyPoints: The $(-1)^n$ in the sine family is the single most commonly dropped mark in this chapter — sin has two adjustments per period, so it needs it; cosine carries ±, tangent neither.
Always reduce the equation to = sinα / cosα / tanα first; solving it before that reduction is where extra invalid roots enter.
summary: Trigonometric Equations and General Values covers essential principles and applications.
